title: Lightweight Kubernetes for the Edge
description: K3s (Rancher) and MicroK8s (Canonical) are lightweight Kubernetes distributions that run the full orchestration API on small hardware — single binary, low memory, ARM-friendly. They bring containers, scheduling, and self-healing to places full Kubernetes cannot go. The edge gets the same declarative model as the cloud.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: K3s: The Single Binary
description: K3s packs the Kubernetes control plane, kubelet, and containerd into one ~100MB binary with an embedded SQLite (or etcd) datastore — install is one command, upgrade is swapping the binary. Rancher built it for edge and IoT. Simplicity is the feature.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: MicroK8s: The Snap Distribution
description: MicroK8s delivers Kubernetes as a snap with opinionated addons — DNS, storage, ingress, GPU — toggled by single commands. Canonical aims it at workstations, edge, and appliances. Addons make the common edge stack one-liners.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Air-Gapped Installation
description: Air-gapped K3s/MicroK8s install from pre-staged binaries and private registries — no internet at deploy time, ever. Images get mirrored into the enclave; manifests reference the mirror. The cluster is born offline and stays offline. Planning the bundle is the work.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Private Registries in the Enclave
description: Harbor or a simple registry mirror serves images inside the air gap, with the cluster's image pull secrets pointing at it. Every image is scanned before mirroring. The registry is the enclave's app store — curated, versioned, offline.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: HA: etcd Quorums at the Edge
title: HA: etcd Quorums at the Edge
description: High-availability K3s runs embedded etcd across 3+ nodes — quorum survives a node loss, which is the point at the edge where hardware fails. MicroK8s clusters similarly with dqlite. Odd numbers, watched disks, tested failover. Edge HA is the same math, harsher conditions.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Kine and Datastore Options
description: K3s's Kine layer lets the control plane use SQLite, Postgres, or etcd as its datastore — SQLite for single nodes, etcd for HA. The choice trades operational simplicity against scale. Defaults are sensible; overrides are available.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Networking: Flannel, Calico, Cilium
description: Edge clusters network with Flannel (simple overlay), Calico (policy-rich), or Cilium (eBPF-powered) — the CNI choice sets the security and observability posture. Air-gapped clusters often add strict network policies by default. Packets follow policy.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Storage at the Edge
description: Edge storage uses local-path provisioners, Longhorn (replicated block), or OpenEBS — persistence without a SAN. Longhorn replicates volumes across nodes so a dead node does not take the data. The edge stores what it must, replicates what matters.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Workload Scheduling and Taints
description: Taints, tolerations, and affinity place workloads deliberately — GPU jobs on GPU nodes, critical pods spread across failure domains. The scheduler is policy execution. At the edge, every node counts, so placement is explicit.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: GitOps in Disconnected Environments
description: GitOps (Flux/Argo) works air-gapped against in-enclave git mirrors — desired state versioned, drift corrected, audits automatic. The repo is the control plane's memory. Disconnected does not mean unmanaged.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Observability: Metrics and Logs
description: Edge clusters run Prometheus/Grafana and Loki-class logging in-cluster — metrics and logs without phoning home. Alerts route to local operators. Observability stays inside the enclave because the data never leaves.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Security Hardening: CIS Benchmarks
description: Hardened K3s/MicroK8s follow CIS Kubernetes benchmarks — RBAC locked down, pod security standards, secrets encrypted at rest, API server flags set. Hardening guides are checklists, not suggestions. The edge is attacked too.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Upgrades Without Internet
description: Air-gapped upgrades stage new binaries and images into the enclave, then roll nodes one by one — the same rolling discipline, offline. Version skew policies still apply. Planned, staged, reversible.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Air-Gapped Cluster Picture
description: Ladder-top edge Kubernetes: light distros, offline install, mirrored images, etcd HA, strict networking, replicated storage, GitOps-managed. Fifteen rungs from a single binary to a tactical cluster that runs disconnected for months.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
